## Personality

Grand, nostalgic and fond of his own voice. He tells the same stories often but tells them well.

## Lore

Thaddeus is a retired captain, and he spends his days on a bench by the water on the Waterfront, where he can see every boat in the bay and comment on all of them. He is seventy-nine, grand, nostalgic and fond of his own voice. He tells the same stories often, but he tells them well, with his hat pushed back and one hand drawing the course in the air, and even people who have heard them a dozen times tend to stop and listen to the end.

### The Cormorant

Thaddeus went to sea as a boy and was master of his own coasting ship, the Cormorant, for thirty years. She was a handsome, fast, slightly vain ship, he says, much like her captain, and he ran timber, salt and anything else that paid along the coast of Veligor. He gave up command at sixty-five, fourteen years ago, and sold the Cormorant to a captain from another harbour, who still sails her. He does not like to talk about that, which makes it the only subject he does not like to talk about.

He was married for forty years to Loveday, who mended sails on the Waterfront and was the only person in Bain Harbour who could make him stop talking by raising one eyebrow. She died ten years ago. Since then Thaddeus has lived alone in a little house a few steps from his bench, and the bench, the bay and the young sailors passing it have become his company.

### The race

The story everyone has heard is the race. Thirty-three years ago, Thaddeus skippered Bain Harbour's boat in the summer race around Veligor. He was forty-six, at the top of his powers, and he had wanted the helm for twenty years. So had Captain Annis of the Saltlark. They had been rivals since they were young sailors racing each other across the bay at every chance, and that summer they quarrelled so long and so loudly over who should skipper the race boat that the council very nearly gave it to someone else to shut them both up. In the end the helm went to Thaddeus.

He led for most of the way around the island. He tells you about every headland, every squall and every sail change. Then, in the last mile, the wind dropped where he was and held where Goa Harbour's boat was, and Goa crossed the line a boat's length ahead. He never skippered the race again; the next summer the helm went to another captain. He never had it again, and Annis never had it at all.

Annis has told him ever since that she would have won. Thaddeus says she would have lost by two. They have had this argument several hundred times, on his bench, at the Salt and Bread and once across a whole council meeting, and both of them would be lost without it. He thinks she is the finest sailor in the harbour. He would rather lose by ten lengths than tell her so.

### The coach

Thaddeus coaches young sailors from his bench whether they asked or not. Most hurry past. His current project is Lowen, the fisherman's son, who has just signed on as a deckhand on the Heron and wants a place on this summer's race crew. Thaddeus has decided the boy has the makings of a racing sailor and tells him so, along with a great deal about trimming sails, reading wind on the water and never trusting a calm in the last mile. Lowen has started taking the long way round. Thaddeus has noticed, and has also noticed that Lowen's knots and sail-handling have improved in exactly the ways he said they should. He is enormously pleased and has told nobody.

Lorcan, the shanty singer, has lately been buying him a drink in exchange for the story of the race, for a verse in his new shanty. Thaddeus has told it to him four times, with a different wind each time.

### What he wants and fears

Thaddeus wants to see Bain Harbour win the race by more than a boat's length, and to have had a hand in it, even from a bench. He fears that he will be remembered only for the one he lost, and, though he would never say so, that the sea he raced on is not the sea out there now.

### Hooks

A quest could find the old logbook from Thaddeus's race and the inshore course he swears would have won it, settle his argument with Annis with a race across the bay between two old captains, or help him find out where the Cormorant is sailing now.
